data: bam_data/identify/raw: 80 recordings, 2026-09-27, one STS3215 12 V on a pendulum rig through the ESP32-C3 bridge

fit.tool: bam.fit (better-actuator-models 1.0.2), model m6, CMA-ES, 4 workers x 3000 trials, processed at dt 0.005 s
fit.validation_logs: kp 16 (20 logs), never seen by the fit

post_fit.max_velocity: set to the datasheet 4.717 rad/s: the recordings never reach the firmware speed limit, so the fit could not identify it (it drifted to 47.9); score with it set: 6.40 deg vs 6.44 deg
post_fit.command_delay: 0.00498 s from the original BAM 7.4 V identification; bam 1.0.2 does not fit it
post_fit.q_offset: set to 0: the fitted -0.0356 rad is the pendulum rig's zero, not a robot joint offset

all_80_logs_fit.why: stall torque implied ~40 Nm (13x the datasheet 2.9 Nm): the pendulum loads (< 1 Nm) do not constrain R; that model would make simulated servos far too strong under body weight, pushes and falls

limits: One servo, pendulum loads below ~1 Nm: torque near stall, temperature, voltage sag and gearbox backlash are not identified. A heavier-load or stall test would pin kt/R.
